fullPassage: Take time to be bored. One time I heard a coworker say, "When I get busy, I get stupid." Ain't that the truth. Creative people need time to just sit around and do nothing. I get some of my best ideas when I'm bored, which is why I never take my shirts to the cleaners. I love ironing my shirts — it's so boring, I almost always get good ideas. If you're out of ideas, wash the dishes. Take a really long walk. Stare at a spot on the wall for as long as you can. As the artist Maira Kalman says, "Avoiding work is the way to focus my mind." Take time to mess around. Get lost. wander. You never know where it's going to lead you.

questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 위 빈칸에 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 명사 people을 수식하는 형용사가 필요: create(동사) → Creative(형용사).
det.analysis:
✅ 정답: Creative
명사 people 앞에서 수식하므로 형용사 형태. 동사 create의 형용사형은 creative.
det.tip: 동사→형용사: create → creative / imagine → imaginative / invent → inventive

questions.passage: I love ironing my shirts — it's so boring, I almost always get good ideas. As the artist Maira Kalman says, "__________ (avoid) work is the way to focus my mind."
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 위 빈칸에 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 주어 자리에서 '~하는 것'을 의미하는 동명사: avoid → Avoiding.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답: Avoiding
문장의 주어 역할(~ is the way to ...)을 하므로 동명사 형태. avoid → Avoiding.
det.tip: 동명사(V-ing)가 주어로 쓰이면 '~하는 것' — Avoiding work = 일을 피하는 것

questions.passage: Take time to be bored. One time I heard a coworker say, "When I get busy, I get stupid." Ain't that the truth. Creative people need time to just sit around and do nothing. I get some of my best ideas when I'm bored, which is why ____. I love ironing my shirts — it's so boring, I almost always get good ideas. If you're out of ideas, wash the dishes. Take a really long walk. Stare at a spot on the wall for as long as you can. As the artist Maira Kalman says, "Avoiding work is the way to focus my mind." Take time to mess around. Get lost. Wander. You never know where it's going to lead you.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 지루할 때 최고의 아이디어를 얻으니까 → '셔츠를 세탁소에 맡기지 않는다'(직접 다림질 = 지루한 활동).
det.analysis:
✅ ① I never take my shirts to the cleaners — 지루할 때 아이디어 = 직접 다림질하는 이유.
❌ ② I always hire a professional cleaner — 전문가 고용은 반대.
❌ ③ I avoid doing housework — 가사 회피는 글 취지와 반대.
❌ ④ I prefer to buy new shirts instead — 새 셔츠 구매는 무관.
det.tip: which is why ~: ~하는 이유 — 직접 다림질(지루한 활동)이 아이디어 원천

ch: I never take my shirts to the cleaners
I always hire a professional cleaner
I prefer to buy new shirts instead

questions.passage: Take time to be bored. One time I heard a coworker say, "When I get busy, I get stupid." Ain't that the truth. Creative people need time to just sit around and do nothing. If you're out of ideas, wash the dishes. Take a really long walk. Stare at a spot on the wall for as long as you can. As the artist Maira Kalman says, "Avoiding work is the way to focus my mind." Take time to mess around. Get lost. Wander. ____.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 헤매라(Wander) 뒤에 오는 마무리: '어디로 이끌지 결코 알 수 없다'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① You should always plan your route carefully — '경로를 계획하라'는 Wander와 모순.
❌ ② Make sure to arrive at your destination on time — '정시 도착'은 정처 없이 돌아다님과 반대.
✅ ③ You never know where it's going to lead you — 어디로 이끌지 모른다는 마무리.
❌ ④ Always return to where you started — '출발점 복귀'는 맥락과 안 맞음.
det.tip: 글 전체 메시지: 지루함·방황의 가치 → 어디로 이끌지 모르지만 그것이 핵심

ch: You should always plan your route carefully
Make sure to arrive at your destination on time
You never know where it's going to lead you
Always return to where you started
